verdict.rationale: Logseq is documented as an open-source, privacy-first knowledge base. Users confirm it keeps data local with source available, and they handle sync and backup themselves via GitHub. Graphs can also be published as a static single-page app. However, one community report says you cannot self-host Logseq as a server-side web app that saves notes to your own server, and that this remains an open feature request. Self-hosting is therefore limited to running the open-source desktop app locally plus static publishing. Missing for 10: a documented self-hosted server/web deployment, a self-hostable sync backend, and first-party self-hosting docs.
